## 3. Two-phase operation flow

Phase 1 — prepare:
- API: `POST /api/v1/operations/prepare` → strict JSON body (`decodeStrictJSON`: requires `Content-Type: application/json`, `DisallowUnknownFields`, exactly one JSON value — operation_handlers.go:593-608) → kind mapping/validation `mapOperationRequest` (:610-742; 27 kinds incl. QA shard-only rules :733-740) → `hub.ops.PrepareOperation` → `preparations.issue(sessionID, confirmation)` → response `preparationDTO{preparation_id, operation, affected_paths, mutation_class, runtime?, harness?, prerequisites, input_fingerprint, expires_at, confirmation_token}` (operation_handlers.go:78-120; DTO :60-71).
- Token record: `preparationRecord{ID "prep_…" , Token "confirm_…", Session, Canonical, Fingerprint, Confirmation, ExpiresAt}` (security.go:368-410); TTL 2min, cap 128 (`PreparationTTL`/`MaxPreparations` operations.go:20-21).

Phase 2 — start consumes the token:
- API: `POST /api/v1/operations` requires non-empty token (operation_handlers.go:142-145); handler re-runs `PrepareOperation` to obtain *current* `CanonicalRequest`/`InputFingerprint`, then `startConfirmed(session, confirmationDedupKey(session,token), consume(token, session, current.Canonical, current.Fingerprint))` (:146-158). `consume` enforces single-use, expiry, session binding, canonical match, fingerprint match — distinct errors `errConfirmationExpired/Mismatch/Replayed/StaleConfirmation` (security.go:413-437, 453-458); stale ⇒ 409 `stale_confirmation`. Dedup key = SHA-256(session||token) makes double-click idempotent while the record lives (security.go:448-451; hub dedup map operations.go:154-159, 209-211).
- Hub start: capacity/drain checks, optional `DurableOperationManager.AcceptOperation` (idempotent durable acceptance; existing run returns early with refresh path) then goroutine `run()` → `ops.RunOperation` with event callback (operations.go:150-243).
- HTML mirror: `/operations/prepare` renders `page/operation-confirm` with hidden `confirmation_token` + spec fields (operation_handlers.go:293-328; template operation-confirm.html:15-25); `/operations/start` performs the same consume (:330-360) and 303-redirects to `/operations/{id}`.

**Mutations WITHOUT the confirmation-token flow** (verified):
1. `POST /projects/{p}/sprints/create` → `handleSprintCreate` (handlers.go:1314-1334): checks `_csrf` form value against session CSRF (:1315), validates slug/project as single safe segments (:1325-1328), then directly invokes `WebSprintWorkspaceMutation.CreateSprintWorkspace` (:1329) which materializes the sprint directory via `dashboard.sprintService().CreateWorkspace(project, slug)` (web_usecases.go:766-775) and 303-redirects to the sprint page (:1333). No `PrepareOperation`, no fingerprint/token. Comment at handlers.go:1312-1313 describes it as materializing the workspace "without running any flow stage". Interface declared additive at web_usecases.go:70-75. Tests: `TestSprintCreateCreatesWorkspaceAndRedirectsToSprintPage` / `TestSprintCreateSurfacesCreationFailure` (sprint_create_test.go:13-55) confirm CSRF/400/422 behavior.
2. `DELETE /api/v1/runs/{id}` → `handleRunCancel` (run_handlers.go:918-929): direct `runs.CancelRun(reason="user_requested")`, no preparation step (middleware CSRF/session still apply).
3. `POST /runs/{id}/cancel` and `POST /operations/{id}/cancel` (HTML): `_csrf` form check only, direct cancel (run_handlers.go:889-903; operation_handlers.go:381-409). Cancellation arguably doesn't need a mutation-fingerprint, but it is outside the two-phase design.

## 4. SSE

Transient (in-process hub) — `GET /api/v1/operations/{id}/events`, `handleOperationEvents` (operation_handlers.go:230-291):
- **Resume/gap honesty**: `Last-Event-ID` header parsed by `parseEventID` (operations.go:660-669). `subscribe` replays retained events with `ID > lastID` from the per-op bounded ring (`MaxEventsPerOperation=256`, `MaxEventBytesPerOperation=256KiB`, eviction loop operations.go:452-455). If `lastID < oldestRetained-1`, it appends a **`recovery_required`** event carrying `{oldest_retained_id, newest_retained_id, refresh_path}` followed by a fresh `snapshot` (operations.go:388-396; counter `replayGaps` :129). Slow subscribers are dropped (channel full ⇒ close, counter `slowSubscribers`) rather than blocking (operations.go:457-467).
- **Frame format**: `writeSSEEvent` → `id: <decimal>\nevent: <name>\ndata: <json>\n\n` (operation_handlers.go:588-591). Event names normalized through `stableOperationEventName` to the closed set `{snapshot, progress, warning, finding, artifact, cancel_requested, recovery_required, terminal}` (operations.go:470-477).
- **Envelope/payload shape**: `{operation_id, time(RFC3339Nano), sequence, payload:{state, stage, task, message, completed, total, attempt, event_kind, event_type, tool, action, tool_call_id, tool_status, tool_arguments, tool_result, tool_error, reason, detail, runtime_attempts, turns, turns_known, tokens, tokens_known, duration, provider, model, harness, cost, runtime_events}}` — envelope built at operations.go:430-436; app-event projection at operations.go:260-270. Oversized events (>16KiB `MaxEncodedEventBytes`) replaced with a `warning` "event projection exceeded the safe size limit" (operations.go:442-448).
- **Heartbeat / lifetime**: `: heartbeat\n\n` comment frames every `SSEHeartbeat = 15s`; hard lifetime `MaxStreamLifetime = 30min` enforced both by timer and `http.NewResponseController.SetWriteDeadline(now+MaxStreamLifetime+SSEHeartbeat)` (operations.go:30-31; operation_handlers.go:254, 265-290).
- **Terminal behavior**: `finish()` marks terminal, closes all subscriber channels (operations.go:303-308); the write loop sees closed channel, flushes, returns (operation_handlers.go:271-274). Client-side reload trigger: browser JS closes the stream on `terminal` and calls `window.location.reload()` (static/app.js:887-894).
- **Durable fallback**: if the hub doesn't know the id, `followDurableOperationEvents` polls `runs.RunEvents(after, 512)` every 250ms–1s until terminal+caught-up, with pre-flight 409 `cursor_ahead` (after > LastSequence) and 409 `replay_gap` (after+1 < OldestRetainedSequence) responses (operation_handlers.go:447-514). Durable event types map to stable names via `durableOperationEvent` (`accepted/claimed/lifecycle→snapshot`, `warning/finding/artifact/terminal` pass through, `cancellation→cancel_requested`, `recovery/omission→recovery_required`), payload `{stage, task, payload, omission}` (operation_handlers.go:516-534). Pre-durable ids (`op_*` prefix, `legacyOperationID` :422) get 410 `legacy_operation_not_retained` on status/events/cancel (operation_handlers.go:174-178, 240-244, 214-218).

Run timelines — `GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/events` (run_handlers.go:931-1047):
- Cursor from `Last-Event-ID` header XOR `?after=` (both ⇒ 400 `cursor_conflict` :943-946). 409 `cursor_ahead` includes requested/last/run snapshot; 409 `replay_gap` includes recovery hints `["refresh_snapshot","resume_from_oldest"]` (:968-980).
- Non-SSE Accept ⇒ one JSON page `{run, events}` (≤512 events) (:981-989). SSE mode `followRunSSE`: frames are `event: run` with `data:` = the **entire marshaled `runcontrol.Event`** (sequence, attempt_id, type, stage, task, committed_at, payload map…) (:1014-1023); heartbeat on idle (1s idle timer when caught-up, 250ms when behind) (:1032-1045); stops on terminal lifecycle && after ≥ LastSequence (:1029-1031). Client: `preflightDurableRun` JSON replay first (handling 409 replay_gap messaging), then `EventSource(...?after=N)`, stops at `event.type === "terminal"` without page reload (app.js:1661-1717).

## 7. Artifacts serving (`internal/web/artifacts.go` + upstream query)

- `artifacts.go` is small (21 lines): `validateArtifact(result app.WebArtifactPreview)` enforces media ∈ {text/markdown, application/json}, `0 ≤ ReturnedBytes ≤ WebPreviewByteLimit`, `len(Content)==ReturnedBytes`, `SizeBytes ≥ ReturnedBytes`, and `Truncated ⇔ SizeBytes > ReturnedBytes` (artifacts.go:9-21). Called before rendering/serving previews (handlers.go:608, 724).
- Actual resolution lives in the app layer, `webUseCases.Artifact(ref)` (web_usecases.go:1300-1347):
  - **Opaque ref resolution**: refs are HMAC-SHA256 (per-process random secret, `u.secret [32]byte`) base64url digests over `(kind, values...)`, stored in an in-memory map at issue time (`issue`, web_usecases.go:1503-1516; resolve :1518-1523). Unknown/kind-mismatched refs ⇒ ErrWebNotFound.
  - **Allowlist**: `supportedPreviewPath(rel)` (usecases.go:214-242) permits only named planning artifacts (project-index.md, roadmap.md, requirements.md, code-context.md, sprint-index.md, technical-handbook.md, reasoning.md, plan.md, execute.md, review.md, smoke.md, flow-state.json, .run-state.json), `projects/*/docs/*.md`, `studies/*/{dimensions,sources,reports}/*.md`, `studies/*/.ultraplan/run-state.json`.
  - **Symlink containment**: `containedArtifactPath` = `workspace.ResolveInside(u.root, rel)` then `filepath.EvalSymlinks` on both root and candidate path, then `filepath.Rel` containment rejecting `..` prefixes ("artifact escapes workspace") (web_usecases.go:1525-1543; workspace.ResolveInside internal/workspace/paths.go:9). Regular-file stat required (web_usecases.go:1324-1327).
  - **Read bound**: `io.LimitReader(file, 256KiB+1)`; truncated flag computed (:1328-1335).
  - **Content types**: `mediaTypeForPath` — `.json` ⇒ `application/json`, everything else `text/markdown` (web_usecases.go:1545-1550). Browser-facing transport is either JSON preview envelopes (`application/json; charset=utf-8`, handlers.go:1110) or server-rendered HTML with markdown converted via `RenderSafeMarkdown`; there is **no raw file-download endpoint** in this surface.

CLI has no study-cancel verb. --- ## 7. Observation convergence Underneath everything sits the same repository via `repositoryRunUseCases` (run_usecases.go:39-57); CLI `run *` commands call the repository directly through the same handle (`runRepository` run_commands.go:42-59 → `deps.runControl.repository`, cached per workspace root run_control.go:46-51). - List: CLI default limit 50 (`fs.Int`, run_commands.go:69 — **no visible upper clamp in the CLI layer**; unverified whether the repository clamps), web clamps 1..200 (run_handlers.go:259-267), TUI fixed 200 (app.go:366). - Detail: identical snapshot; web joins study insights / sprint usage / QA insights onto the page (run_handlers.go:352-371) — enrichment absent in CLI/TUI. - Follow/streaming: CLI poller (run_commands.go:161-194) and web SSE `followRunSSE` (run_handlers.go:993-1047) are near-identical algorithms (512-batch, 250ms backfill / 1s idle, terminal+lastSequence exit). Web additionally has the durable-operation SSE projection (`followDurableOperationEvents`, operation_handlers.go:447-514) mapping event types → stable names (`durableOperationEvent` :516-534). TUI re-fetches ≤200 events per 1-second tick instead of streaming (app.go:222-226, 271-273, 380-387). - Formats: CLI human text (`renderRunSnapshot` run_commands.go:416-425) or `jsonEnvelope` (json_output.go:11-31); web `{data, meta}` JSON envelopes plus server-rendered HTML; TUI rendered strings (views.go:11+). Omissions surfaced in all three (formatEventOmission run_commands.go:437-442; runEventView.Omission run_handlers.go:727-742; TUI dedup of repeated omissions run_view_test.go:44-56). --- ## 8. Identity/context resolution Single resolution path for all interfaces: `discoverWorkspace` (app.go:287-298) = `workspace.Discover{ExplicitPath: --workspace flag (parsed once in app.Run, app.go:134, 198-220), EnvWorkspace: ULTRAPLAN_WORKSPACE, StartDir: deps.workDir (os.Getwd fallback app.go:128-132)}`. Serve adds **no** cwd-relative or config override of its own — `configOverridesForServe` returns the zero value explicitly (serve_commands.go:110-115). Process-wide effect: because `runControlState` caches repos keyed by root (run_control.go:46-51) and rejects mid-process retention-policy changes (:47-49), a single process serving TUI or web holds exactly one pool per resolved workspace. --- ## 9. Failure surfacing - **Classification origin**: `failedOperation` (operations.go:751-796) maps smoke errors (`sprint.AsSmokeError` :759-764), QA errors (:765-780), sentinel/reference errors and findings (:781-792) into `OperationError{Code, Category, Guidance, Retryable}` (:204-207); public-query QA failures are re-wrapped as redacted `QAUseCaseError` (qa_errors.go:42-56). Text is scrubbed by `safeProjectedText` (operations.go:634-651). - **TUI rendering**: no dialogs — inline banner `Error: ...` in the header (views.go:23-24), parallel-form field error (:66-67), and structured operation failure rendering Code/Category/Retryable/Guidance (:424-425); findings rendered `[severity] section: problem / Cause / Guidance` (model_test.go:148-157 confirms format). --- ## Flagged / unverified - Web UI reachability of `study-cancel`: mapped and contract-tested, but no template/static-JS issuer found in this tree. - CLI `run list --limit`: no upper bound enforced at the flag-parse layer; repository-side clamping not traced. - `sprint qa cancel` ownership precheck (sprint_usecases.go:728-730) exists only on that CLI/ad-hoc path; generic web/TUI run cancel performs no such target validation (fact of asymmetry, severity not assessed here). - Whether any consumer depends on the web form's `study_run_loop` → `OperationStudyStart` vs CLI/TUI's unconditional `OperationStudyResume` distinction is not determinable from code alone.

# UltraPlan Go — CLI Grammar/Contract Mechanics (frozen @ f0fcd0c)

Tree root: `/tmp/opencode/upgo-frozen` (paths below relative to it). Line numbers verified against this checkout.

## Q1. Command dispatch — `internal/app/app.go`

**Entry wiring**
- `cmd/ultraplan/main.go:18-43` — `main()` builds `signal.NotifyContext` (SIGINT/SIGTERM), calls `os.Exit(app.Run(app.Config{Args: os.Args[1:], Stdout/Stderr: os.Stdout/os.Stderr, Context, Version: app.DefaultVersion(), TUIRunner, WebRunner}))`.
- `app.Run(cfg Config) int` — `internal/app/app.go:88-178`. Nil writers default to `io.Discard` (89-97), stdin defaults to `os.Stdin` (98-101); zero version falls back to `DefaultVersion()` (`version.go:18-25`, values `0.0.0-local/local/local` + `runtime.Version()`).

**Global `--workspace` parsing**
- `parseGlobalFlags` — `app.go:198-220`: scans **the entire argv**, not just leading flags; recognizes both `--workspace <path>` (204-209, rejects missing value or value starting with `-`) and `--workspace=<path>` (210-214, rejects empty). All other tokens are passed through in order.
- Result stored in `deps.workspaceFlag` (`app.go:138`, field `app.go:186`). Note: because parsing is global-position, `ultraplan serve --workspace X` works (pinned by `serve_commands_test.go:32`).
- `discoverWorkspace(deps)` — `app.go:287-298` → `workspace.Discover` (`internal/workspace/discovery.go:21-51`). Precedence: explicit flag (`discovery.go:22-24`) → env `ULTRAPLAN_WORKSPACE` (25-27) → cwd-ancestry walk upward until a dir containing marker `ultraplan.yml` (28-49, `MarkerFile` at :9). Failure text: `"workspace not found: initialize one with 'ultraplan init-workspace'"` (:50).
- Env lookup: `envLookup` — `app.go:300-307`; uses injected `cfg.Env` map if non-nil, else `os.Getenv`.
- WorkDir: `cfg.WorkDir` or `os.Getwd()` (`app.go:128-132`).
- Divergence (neutral): `defaults install` and `skills materialise` consume `deps.workspaceFlag` **directly as a filesystem path** without discovery/env/marker validation (`defaults_commands.go:26-29`, `skills_commands.go:26-29`); `init-workspace` uses `deps.workDir` (`workspace_commands.go:11`).

**Dispatch table** — `app.go:144-177`: first-arg switch over `--help/-h`, `version`, `init-workspace`, `defaults`, `skills`, `config`, `health`, `storage`, `run`, `project`, `sprint`, `study`, `tui`, `serve`, `code`. Each command gets `args[1:]`.

**Unknown command** — `app.go:175-177`: `classified(ExitUsage, "unknown command %q\n\nRun 'ultraplan --help' to see available commands.", args[0])` → stderr, exit 2 (pinned by `app_test.go:72-83`).

**Help/version output paths**
- No args → `writeStatus(stdout, renderHelp())` exit 0 (`app.go:140-142`).
- `--help`/`-h` as first arg → help on stdout (`app.go:145-146`). There is **no `--version` flag**; only the `version` subcommand (`app.go:147-148` → `renderVersion` `app.go:278-285`, four lines `Version:/Commit:/BuildDate:/GoVersion:`).
- `renderHelp` — `app.go:250-276` (embedded string listing 13 commands + flags).
- `writeStatus` returns `ExitError` on write failure (`app.go:243-248`); `failOrOK`/`fail` — `app.go:222-241` print `err.Error()` to stderr via `Fprintln` and return `classedError.class` or `ExitError`.

## Q2. Exit-code contract

**Constants** — `app.go:15-25`: `ExitOK=0, ExitError=1, ExitUsage=2, ExitConfig=3, ExitWorkspace=4, ExitValidation=5, ExitRuntime=6, ExitCancel=7, ExitPartial=8`.

**Stable code strings** — `errorCode(class)` `app.go:67-86`: 2→`validation.usage`, 3→`config.invalid`, 4→`validation.workspace`, 5→`validation.reference`, 6→`provider.runtime`, 7→`workflow.cancelled`, 8→`workflow.partial`, default→`internal.error`. `classedError` type `app.go:41-49` (`class/code/err`, exposes `Code()`); constructors `classified`/`classifiedCause` `app.go:59-65`. Matches doc `docs/cli-reference.md:18-31`.

**Per-command error mapping (facts)**

| Mapper | Location | Mapping |
|---|---|---|
| `mapRunControlError` | `run_commands.go:403-414` | `ErrInvalidArgument`→2; `ErrNotFound`→5; `ErrConflict`/`ErrTerminal`→8; default→6 |

## Q3. Output contracts

**Envelope** — `json_output.go:9-32`: `jsonEnvelope{schema_version:int(1), command:string, workspace:string omitempty, status:string, generated_at:time, result:any}`; pretty-printed 2-space indent via `json.Encoder.SetIndent`. **Envelope users** (inline `{schema_version…}` wrapper):

- Errors: always stderr via `fail()` (`app.go:229-241`); findings rendered inline to stderr in several renderers: project validate findings (`project_commands.go:118-129`, pinned `project_commands_test.go:64-84`), run-all non-completed tasks/warnings (`study_commands.go:715-729`), execution failures/validation (`study_commands.go:898-928`), run-loop non-completed tasks (`study_commands.go:386-394`), summary warnings (`study_commands.go:774-780`).

## Q4. Arg-parsing styles (three coexist)

**(a) Hand-rolled loops** — examples:
1. `parseGlobalFlags` (`app.go:198-220`) — whole-argv scan, `--workspace[= ]`.
2. `parseRunLoopArgs` (`study_commands.go:241-275`) — filters bool flags then delegates; and `parseSprintFlowArgs` (`sprint_commands.go:1003-1074`) — index loop with `--to/--model/--variant/--stage-model=/--stage-variant= [--restart-review] [--yes|--non-interactive] [--force-review] [--override-reason] [--dry-run]`.
3. `parseStudyInitArgs` (`study_commands.go:1489-1525`), `parseSprintExecuteArgs` (`sprint_commands.go:1193-1233`, incl. two-token `--defer --reason <text>` :1207-1215), `parseSprintSmokeArgs` (`sprint_commands.go:825-877`), `parseCodeArgs` (`code_commands.go:80-108`), hand loops in `workspace_commands.go:13-29`, `defaults_commands.go:32-50`, `skills_commands.go:34-59`, `storage_commands.go:42-54`, `config_commands.go:22-32`, `health_commands.go:32-42`, `study_commands.go:1013-1024,1113-1124` (validate/status), `project_commands.go` positional grammar, `parseSprintQAArgs` (`sprint_commands.go:588-640`), `stripFlag` (`sprint_commands.go:568-579`).

**(b) stdlib `flag.FlagSet`** — examples:
1. `runList` (`run_commands.go:62-77`) — `--json --project --sprint --study --lifecycle --limit --after`, `SetOutput(io.Discard)`, error+`NArg()!=0`→usage via `firstFlagError` (:453-461).
2. `runServe` (`serve_commands.go:19-34`) — `--listen --open-browser`, custom `fs.Usage` writing help to **stdout** (:23), `flag.ErrHelp`→exit 0 (:25-27).
3. Also `runDiagnostics` (`run_commands.go:230-240`).

**(c) stdlib flag + `orderRunArgs` pre-reorder** — `orderRunArgs(args, valued)` `run_commands.go:463-481`: partitions tokens into flags-first/positionals-last; known flag names are exactly `--json`, `-h`, `--help`, plus caller-supplied `valued` set. Examples: `runShow` (:113, valued=nil), `runFollow` (:140, valued=`{"--after"}`), `runCancel` (:206, valued=`{"--reason"}`).

**Quirks relevant for later review (neutral mechanics)**
- Flags-after-positional: works only in `orderRunArgs` paths and only for the 3 hard-coded names (+valued set); any other dash token (incl. `--`) becomes a **positional** in reorder paths (:469-473), while pure-stdlib paths stop at first non-flag (Go flag semantics). E.g. `run show <id> --limit=5` fails with "expected '<run-id>'".
- Valued-flag consumption in `orderRunArgs` does not check whether the next token starts with `-`: `run follow id --after --json` consumes `--json` as the sequence value (:475-478) → later `ParseUint` usage error.
- Repeated flags: hand loops are last-wins for scalars (`--model`, `--output`, `--path`), append for repeatables (`--dimension/--source/--focus/--focus-review`); stdlib flag is last-wins; `stripFlag` deletes every occurrence of `--json`.
- `--` terminator: meaningful only in pure-stdlib paths (`run list`, `run diagnostics`, `serve`); in reorder/hand paths it's an ordinary positional/unknown arg.
- Help detection is position-sensitive in most families: `helpRequested` scans anywhere for run subcommands (`run_commands.go:444-451`); sprint checks exact slots `args[0]` / `args[3]` given `args[2]` (`sprint_commands.go:32-70`); study run-all/run/run-loop accept help only as sole remaining arg (`study_commands.go:198,547,803`), while study validate/status loops accept it among any args (:1014-1023,:1114-1123).
- Global `--workspace` is stripped even when it appears where a subcommand might want it (single namespace, no escaping mechanism).

## Q5. `run` family — `internal/app/run_commands.go`

- Dispatch `runRun` :19-40 (`list|show|follow|cancel|diagnostics`; unknown→usage :38; help strings `runHelp` :483-496, per-sub `run*Help` :498-510).

## Q1. Command dispatch — `internal/app/app.go`

**Entry wiring**

**Global `--workspace` parsing**
- `parseGlobalFlags` — `app.go:198-220`: scans **the entire argv**, not just leading flags; recognizes both `--workspace <path>` (204-209, rejects missing value or value starting with `-`) and `--workspace=<path>` (210-214, rejects empty). All other tokens are passed through in order.

- `discoverWorkspace(deps)` — `app.go:287-298` → `workspace.Discover` (`internal/workspace/discovery.go:21-51`). Precedence: explicit flag (`discovery.go:22-24`) → env `ULTRAPLAN_WORKSPACE` (25-27) → cwd-ancestry walk upward until a dir containing marker `ultraplan.yml` (28-49, `MarkerFile` at :9). **(c) stdlib flag + `orderRunArgs` pre-reorder** — `orderRunArgs(args, valued)` `run_commands.go:463-481`: partitions tokens into flags-first/positionals-last; known flag names are exactly `--json`, `-h`, `--help`, plus caller-supplied `valued` set. Examples: `runShow` (:113, valued=nil), `runFollow` (:140, valued=`{"--after"}`), `runCancel` (:206, valued=`{"--reason"}`).

**Quirks relevant for later review (neutral mechanics)**
- Flags-after-positional: works only in `orderRunArgs` paths and only for the 3 hard-coded names (+valued set); any other dash token (incl. `--`) becomes a **positional** in reorder paths (:469-473), while pure-stdlib paths stop at first non-flag (Go flag semantics). E.g. `run show <id> --limit=5` fails with "expected '<run-id>'".
- Valued-flag consumption in `orderRunArgs` does not check whether the next token starts with `-`: `run follow id --after --json` consumes `--json` as the sequence value (:475-478) → later `ParseUint` usage error.
- Repeated flags: hand loops are last-wins for scalars (`--model`, `--output`, `--path`), append for repeatables (`--dimension/--source/--focus/--focus-review`); stdlib flag is last-wins; `stripFlag` deletes every occurrence of `--json`.
- `--` terminator: meaningful only in pure-stdlib paths (`run list`, `run diagnostics`, `serve`); in reorder/hand paths it's an ordinary positional/unknown arg.
- Help detection is position-sensitive in most families: `helpRequested` scans anywhere for run subcommands (`run_commands.go:444-451`); sprint checks exact slots `args[0]` / `args[3]` given `args[2]` (`sprint_commands.go:32-70`); study run-all/run/run-loop accept help only as sole remaining arg (`study_commands.go:198,547,803`), while study validate/status loops accept it among any args (:1014-1023,:1114-1123).
- Global `--workspace` is stripped even when it appears where a subcommand might want it (single namespace, no escaping mechanism).

# Accessibility Contract

## Purpose

This contract defines the minimum accessibility requirements for frontend and UI changes.

It governs:

- semantic HTML and ARIA
- keyboard interaction
- focus management
- forms and errors
- color/contrast and visual states
- motion
- screen reader support
- accessible testing and review

## Scope

This contract applies when a change:

- adds or changes UI components, pages, flows, forms, dialogs, navigation, charts, or interactive controls
- changes design-system primitives or patterns
- changes loading/error/empty states
- adds animation or motion

## Requirement Index

| ID | Title | Applies To | Severity If Violated |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A11Y-SEM-001 | UI must use semantic structure before ARIA | all UI | High |
| A11Y-KBD-001 | Interactive UI must work by keyboard | controls/dialogs/nav | Blocker |
| A11Y-FOCUS-001 | Focus management must be deliberate | route/dialog/dynamic UI | High |
| A11Y-FORM-001 | Forms must expose labels, errors, and status accessibly | forms | High |
| A11Y-VIS-001 | Visual states must not rely only on color | UI states | Medium |
| A11Y-MOTION-001 | Motion must respect reduced-motion needs | animation | Medium |
| A11Y-TEST-001 | Critical UI must have accessibility checks | frontend tests/review | Medium |

## Core Principles

- changes generated API documentation or clients

## Core Principles

# Frontend Contract

## Purpose
This contract defines the structural and architectural rules for frontend code in this project.

It governs:
- frontend directory structure
- ownership boundaries between app, pages, features, entities, workflows, shared, and design system
- dependency direction
- state placement strategy
- API boundary handling
- testing and extension discipline

It does not replace the general contracts in `ops/operational-contract/`.
Use those contracts alongside this document for testing, error handling, observability, and broader architectural review.

## Scope
This contract applies when a change:
- creates or edits `frontend/`
- introduces a new frontend route, feature, entity, workflow, or shared utility
- changes frontend state management patterns
- changes frontend API access patterns
- changes frontend design-system boundaries
- adds reusable frontend scaffolding or conventions

## How To Use This Contract
Use this contract in three ways:
- during reasoning, map the applicable requirement IDs to the planned frontend change
- during implementation, place code in the correct ownership boundary and preserve allowed dependencies
- during review, verify the change against the evidence guidance and rejection criteria

## Requirement Index

| ID | Title | Applies To | Severity If Violated |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FE-STRUCT-001 | Frontend structure must follow explicit ownership layers | all frontend additions and edits | High |
| FE-BOUNDARY-001 | Dependency direction must remain constrained | cross-folder imports and architecture changes | Blocker |
| FE-APP-001 | App layer must only compose global runtime concerns | `src/app/` | High |
| FE-PAGE-001 | Pages must stay route-level and thin | `src/pages/` | High |
| FE-FEATURE-001 | Features must own business capabilities vertically | `src/features/` | High |
| FE-ENTITY-001 | Entities must model reusable business objects, not global feature logic | `src/entities/` | Medium |
| FE-WORKFLOW-001 | Cross-feature user journeys must live in workflows | `src/workflows/` | Medium |
| FE-SHARED-001 | Shared code must remain domain-neutral and difficult to expand casually | `src/shared/` | High |
| FE-DS-001 | Design system must stay separate from business behavior | `src/design-system/` | High |
| FE-STATE-001 | State must be placed by responsibility, not convenience | all client state decisions | Blocker |
| FE-API-001 | API access must be explicit, typed, and feature-owned | API calls, DTOs, query hooks, mappers | High |
| FE-TEST-001 | Frontend logic must be testable through stable seams | components, hooks, models, workflows | High |
| FE-EXT-001 | New frontend capabilities must be scaffoldable and consistent | new features and routes | Medium |
| FE-A11Y-001 | UI changes must preserve accessibility | all frontend UI changes | High |
| FE-PERF-001 | Frontend changes must avoid unnecessary render, bundle, and data-fetching cost | all frontend changes | High |
| FE-FORM-001 | Forms must handle validation, pending, success, error, disabled, and retry states consistently | form components and submissions | High |

## Target Structure

The frontend should converge on this structure:

```text
frontend/
├─ public/
├─ src/
===CLI-REST===
| CLI-NONINT-001 | Non-interactive mode must never hang on prompts | CI/automation | High |

## Core Principles

1. CLIs are both user interfaces and automation APIs.
2. Human-readable output and machine-readable output have different contracts.
3. Stdout is for intended command output; stderr is for diagnostics and progress.
4. Exit codes are part of the public interface.
5. Destructive actions must be explicit.
6. Non-interactive execution must be deterministic.
7. Help should teach the user the next step.
8. Shared setup, cancellation, and cleanup behaviour should be centralized and testable.

## Requirements

### CLI-SHAPE-001: Commands And Flags Must Be Predictable And Discoverable

**Rule**
Command names, flags, arguments, and subcommands must follow consistent conventions.

**Required**

# Surface Map — map-05-interface-surfaces (CLI / TUI / web interfaces)

Job: independent product-surface discovery from the interface lens. No findings reported in this phase; risk notes are prioritisation rationale only.

## Provenance

- Target: `/home/antonioborgerees/coding/ultraplan/ultraplan-go`, frozen commit `f0fcd0c2107a8e8d69e1283f9e8d5e2c6da94025`. All discovery ran against a dedicated pinned clone (`/tmp/opencode/upgo-frozen`, verified `git rev-parse` = `f0fcd0c`). The live working tree is at `ad0be98`; sole delta vs frozen is `internal/sprint/prompt_context.go` (256 KiB → 512 KiB shared prompt budget) — not interface code. Everything below holds at both commits.
- Planning workspace: `/home/antonioborgerees/coding/ultraplan/ultraplan-workspace` @ `ab12dc38059c…` (== HEAD). CURRENT-CONTRACT anchors consulted: `system/contracts/surfaces/{cli,api-contracts,accessibility,frontend}.md`.
- Method: 5 parallel bounded `review-worker` discoveries (CLI grammar, TUI, web routes/lifecycle, web security model, interface convergence/divergence) + mapper verification of load-bearing claims (TUI cancel path `internal/tui/app.go:232-269`; `validCommandOrigin` body vs docstring `internal/web/security.go:269-274`; definition-only helpers `security.go:262-267,300-302`; 27-entry operation-kind enum; zero TUI constructions of `sprint-stage`/`sprint-stage-dry-run`/`validate`; no template/JS issuer of web `study-cancel`).
- Baseline: go test / -race / vet / cover all passed at freeze (state.json).

## Interface topology in one paragraph

Three frontends over one app core. `cmd/ultraplan/main.go` injects `TUIRunner`/`WebRunner` function types into `app.Run` (`internal/app/app.go:88-178`, inversion at `surfaces.go:18-20`); nothing in `internal/app` imports the frontends. CLI handlers mostly call product services directly; TUI and web share the `OperationalUseCases` boundary (`dashboardUseCases`) plus `DurableOperationManager` + `repositoryRunUseCases`, with runtime-backed work funnelling through `sharedOperationRunner` (`operation_runner.go:18-169`). One composition root resolves the workspace identically for all three (`discoverWorkspace`, `app.go:287-298`: `--workspace` flag → `ULTRAPLAN_WORKSPACE` → cwd-ancestry marker walk), and one SQLite run-control repository per workspace root backs observation/cancellation everywhere. Divergence lives in grammar (three arg-parsing styles), durability mechanics (CLI accept has empty digest/no dedup alias vs web/TUI fingerprint digests), and capability coverage (web-only sprint create/model list/timeline; CLI-only `code`, diagnostics export, study reset; TUI-only interactive parallelism form).

---

## Candidate surfaces

Grouping proposal: **A CLI shell** (IA1–IA2), **B Web console** (IB1–IB3), **C TUI** (IC1–IC2), **D Cross-interface** (ID1). Overlaps map-01's coarse S10–S12 but splits them into reviewable units.

### IA1 — `cli-dispatch-exit-contract` (domain A)
- Behaviour: argv dispatch of 15 top-level commands (`--help/-h`, `version`, `init-workspace`, `defaults`, `skills`, `config`, `health`, `storage`, `run`, `project`, `sprint`, `study`, `tui`, `serve`, `code`); whole-argv global `--workspace[=]` scan; exit classes 0–8 with stable code strings; three output styles (jsonEnvelope `{schema_version,command,workspace,status,result}`, ad-hoc sprint-family maps, raw structs); help/version text.
- Files: `cmd/ultraplan/main.go`, `internal/app/{app,json_output,status_json,qa_errors}.go`, per-command `*_commands.go` parsers/dispatchers, contract docs `docs/cli-reference.md`.
- Failure semantics: unknown command → exit 2 stderr (`app.go:175-177`); classified causes preserved (`classedError`, `errorCode` `app.go:41-86`).
- Inventory facts for reviewers: error-classification default differs per family (sprint/study/project → 4; run-control → 6); QA cancel/deadline → 8 while sprint cancellation → 7; some sprint CLI paths classify by error-text sniffing (`strings.Contains(err.Error(), "runtime")` → 6, `"failed tasks"` → 8, `sprint_commands.go:269,360-364,507`) whereas the operation-runner path pins no text classification (`failedOperation`, `operations.go:751-796`, pinned by `sprint_error_test.go:29-41`); three arg-parser styles coexist (hand loops, stdlib flag, `orderRunArgs` reorder where an unrecognised dash token becomes positional and a valued-flag swallows a following `--flag` as value, `run_commands.go:463-481`); undocumented surface: `tui`, `storage migrate`, `sprint metrics`, `study runs summary`, flow model/variant override flags, prompt `review`/`--explain`, cancel reason whitelist, `--workspace=` form; embedded `skillsMaterialiseHelp` lists 9 stages while workspace layer defines 11 incl. `reconcile` (`skills_commands.go:119-128` vs `workspace/skills.go:41,231-233`).
- Key tests: `app_test.go` (help/version/unknown/classified cause), `run_commands_test.go`, `sprint_commands_test.go` (exit classes, single JSON failure document, stable QA codes), `study_*_commands_test.go`, `serve_commands_test.go`, `code_commands_test.go` (exit 4/5/8 matrix).
- Seams: every runtime-backed command crosses the durable acceptance seam (`beginDurableCLICommand`, counted by source inventory `run_control_inventory_test.go:11-55`); JSON shapes are the automation contract.
- Risk: normal-high — silent breakage class (exit codes/JSON shapes) consumed by scripts and agents.

### IA2 — `run-cli-observation-control` (domain A)
- Behaviour: `run list|show|follow|cancel|diagnostics` against the shared repository: filtered listing (limit default 50, bounds enforced 1..200 downstream `runcontrol/lifecycle.go:197-202`), snapshot render, follow loop (512-event batches, 250 ms backfill / 1 s idle, exits on terminal && cursor ≥ LastSequence, ctx-cancel leaves durable state untouched), cancel with reason whitelist {user/operator/shutdown/quota}→`RequestCancellation`, diagnostics health block + bounded support export (≤1 MiB, O_EXCL 0600).
- Files: `internal/app/run_commands.go`, `internal/app/run_usecases.go` (`repositoryRunUseCases`), `internal/runcontrol` observation API.
- Key tests: `TestRunCommandsListShowFollowCancelDiagnosticsAndSupport`, `TestRunFollowReplaysTerminalJournalAndStopsWithoutCancelling`, `TestRunHelpDoesNotOpenRepository` (`run_commands_test.go`).
- Seams: same queries as web SSE and TUI polling; same `RequestCancellation` as all interfaces.
- Risk: normal; it is the operator's window into the S9 durable spine.

### IB1 — `web-routing-projection-compat` (domain B)
- Behaviour: hand-rolled route matcher (~47 page/API/static GETs + mutations): HTML pages (dashboard/projects/project/sprint/studies/study/runs/run/artifact/operation/operation-confirm/QA pages), `/api/v1/*` JSON reads with strict param regexes and query-string allowlist, artifact preview via HMAC opaque refs + symlink-evaluated containment + 256 KiB bound, go:embed templates (primitive→component→layout→page hierarchy validated at startup) and 14-name static allowlist; compatibility frozen by executable fixtures.
- Files: `internal/web/{routes,handlers,artifacts}.go`, `templates/**`, `static/**` (server-side parts), `web_usecases.go` projection layer (`bounded[T]`, honest `meta.returned_count/total_count/truncated`), `api_compatibility_test.go`, `routes_test.go`, `packaging_test.go`.
- Failure semantics: unknown query → 400; `/api/v2/*` → 404; wrong method → 405+Allow; internal causes collapsed to generic codes (`writeRouteError`, tested `routes_test.go:185`).
- Key facts: QA API returns raw app structs verbatim (no DTO layer, `qa_handlers.go`); markdown reaches browser only through goldmark-based `RenderSafeMarkdown` (raw HTML omitted, unsafe links filtered, `markdown.go:11-22`); JSON encoding uses `SetEscapeHTML(true)`; `Cache-Control: no-store` globally except static revalidated assets.
- Seams: consumes dashboardUseCases/webUseCases queries; artifact refs minted in-memory per process (restart invalidates).
- Risk: high — largest read/projection surface; escaping posture and envelope stability are review targets.

### IB2 — `web-operation-hub-sse` (domain B)
- Behaviour: two-phase operations (prepare → confirmation_token TTL 2 min, cap 128 → start consuming token against freshly prepared canonical request+fingerprint, atomic consume, sha256(session‖token) dedup for double-click idempotency); hub caps (MaxActiveOperations=8 → 429+Retry-After, streams 32/subscribers-per-op 8, ring 256 events/256 KiB/op, encoded event cap 16 KiB → warning stub); SSE with closed event-name set {snapshot, progress, warning, finding, artifact, cancel_requested, recovery_required, terminal}, Last-Event-ID replay, `recovery_required` on replay gap, slow-subscriber drop, 30 min lifetime/15 s heartbeat; graceful drain (reject new starts, cancel non-terminal ops reason `server_shutdown`, deadline → persist cleanup-uncertain markers via `RecordOperationCleanupUncertain`, project `cleanup_uncertain` terminal state).
